### 4. Best Practices for AI-Generated Merchandise Designs

#### Resolution Requirements

| Product | Print Area | Required Resolution (300 DPI) |
|---|---|---|
| T-shirt (front) | 12" x 16" | 3600 x 4800 px |
| T-shirt (back) | 12" x 16" | 3600 x 4800 px |
| Hoodie (chest) | ~10" x 6" | 3000 x 1800 px |
| Hat (front) | ~2.5" x 2.5" | 1200 x 1200 px (embroidery) |
| Mug (wrap) | 9.5" x 3.5" | 2850 x 1050 px |

**The fundamental problem**: Most AI models output at 1024x1024. For t-shirts you need 3600x4800. This is a 4.7x upscale requirement.

**Recommended pipeline**:
1. Generate at 1024x1024 (fast, cheap)
2. Remove background (rembg/Bria)
3. Upscale 4x with ESRGAN to 4096x4096
4. Let the user position on canvas at the correct aspect ratio
5. Export production PNG at target resolution from the canvas (our `exportProductionPNG` already does this)

#### Transparent Background Handling

**Best practice**: Never rely on the AI model to generate transparency. Always use a dedicated background removal step.

The ideal pipeline:
1. Prompt engineering: Include "isolated on solid white background, clean edges" in the prompt (this makes BG removal much cleaner)
2. Post-generation: Run through Bria RMBG 2.0 or rembg
3. Quality check: Verify alpha channel edges are clean (no halo artifacts)

Our prompt engineer at `/Users/lr0y/POD-AI-PDR/pod_workspace/project/frontend/src/lib/providers/prompt-engineer.ts` already appends `", isolated on solid background, clean edges, print-ready, high resolution"` -- this is correct.

#### Common Pitfalls

1. **Text generation quality**: AI models struggle with readable text. For typography-heavy designs, Ideogram V3 (text quality: 5/5) or manual text via Fabric.js IText is far superior. Our router already prioritizes Ideogram for `text-heavy` intent.

2. **Color bleeding at edges**: AI-generated images often have soft gradients at subject edges that create "halos" when placed on different colored garments. Solution: aggressive BG removal + 1-2px edge contraction.

3. **Garment-inappropriate designs**: A photorealistic landscape looks great on screen but prints poorly on a t-shirt. Prompt engineering should include product context. Our orchestrator already does this: `"${prompt}, suitable for ${productType} print"`.

4. **Resolution artifacts after upscaling**: ESRGAN can introduce artifacts on certain patterns. For vector/flat designs, Recraft V3 (native SVG output) avoids this entirely.

5. **Print bleed and safe zones**: Designs must stay within the print area with margin for error. Our CanvasWorkspace already implements `clampObjectToPrintArea` and `drawSafeZone`.

## 6. Scalable Architecture

### Module-Based Structure

The current admin uses Next.js App Router with `(dashboard)` route group. Recommended structure:

```
admin/src/
  app/(dashboard)/
    [module]/
      page.tsx          -- List view
      [id]/page.tsx     -- Detail view
      new/page.tsx      -- Create view
      _components/      -- Module-specific components
      _hooks/           -- Module-specific hooks
      _types.ts         -- Module-specific types
  hooks/
    queries/            -- React Query hooks per module (useOrders already exists)
  contexts/             -- Global contexts (NotificationsContext exists)
  lib/
    admin-api.ts        -- Admin API client (exists)
```

### RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)

| Component | Description |
|---|---|
| **Roles** | `super_admin`, `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`, `support` |
| **Permission model** | `role -> permission -> resource:action` (e.g., `admin -> orders:read`, `admin -> orders:update`, `editor -> products:create`) |
| **Middleware guard** | Next.js middleware checks JWT token, extracts role, blocks unauthorized routes |
| **Component-level guards** | `<RequirePermission permission="orders:update">` wrapper component hides UI elements |
| **API-level guards** | Every API route validates role before processing (server-side enforcement) |
| **Supabase RLS integration** | Admin roles stored in `user_metadata`, RLS policies reference role field |
| **Audit trail** | Log who did what, when -- every write operation creates an audit log entry |

### Real-Time Updates

| Approach | When to Use | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| **SSE (Server-Sent Events)** | Activity feed, notifications, order status updates | Next.js API route with `ReadableStream`, client uses `EventSource` |
| **Polling (React Query)** | Dashboard stats, cron status, sync status | `refetchInterval: 30000` on React Query hooks |
| **Webhooks (incoming)** | Stripe events, Printful status changes | Already have webhook endpoints -- surface events to admin via SSE |

SSE is recommended over WebSockets for this admin because all real-time flows are server-to-client (unidirectional). SSE works over standard HTTP, needs no extra infrastructure, and is natively supported by browsers.

### Caching Strategy

| Layer | Tool | TTL | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Client** | React Query | 30s-5min | Dedup requests, show stale data while revalidating |
| **Server** | Redis | 1-10min | Cache expensive queries (analytics aggregations, product counts) |
| **CDN** | Caddy/Cloudflare | 5-60min | Static assets, brand images |
| **API responses** | `Cache-Control` headers | Varies | `stale-while-revalidate` pattern for admin API responses |

## Key Architectural Recommendations

1. **Standardize on TanStack Table** -- Replace raw `<Table>` usage with TanStack Table (already the standard for React data tables). It provides sorting, filtering, pagination, column visibility, row selection, and virtual scrolling out of the box. 2. **SSE for real-time** -- Add a single `/api/admin/events` SSE endpoint that multiplexes events (new order, sync status change, error alert, webhook received). The `TopBar` component subscribes once and dispatches to notification center, activity feed, and dashboard widgets.

3. **React Query everywhere** -- The orders page already uses React Query via `useOrders`. Extend this pattern to all pages. Create `useProducts`, `useCustomers`, `useDesigns`, `useSyncStatus`, etc. in `hooks/queries/`.

4. **Standardize page layout** -- Every admin page should follow: Breadcrumbs -> Title + Actions -> Filter bar -> Content (table or cards) -> Pagination. Create a `<PageLayout>` component that enforces this.
